subject: general
question: Sameer has a solid metal ball having a diameter of 6 cm. He melts it and uses the material for making a solid cylinder. If the diameter of the base of the cylinder is same as that of the ball, what would the height of the cylinder be?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **sphere** is melted into a **cylinder** of the same **radius** (r), their volumes are equal.

(4/3) × π × r³ = π × r² × h

This simplifies to: **h = (4/3) × r**

Given **diameter** = 6 cm ⇒ **radius** (r) = 3 cm.

Height (h) = (4/3) × 3 = 4 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the **metal ball** (sphere) = 6 cm

Diameter of the **cylinder base** = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **Sphere** = (4/3) π r³

Volume of **Cylinder** = π r² h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acf283fd5b556c7022c0c85d791928b3ee2504cc280b095a770783d6a51275f7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius of sphere (r) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Radius of cylinder base (R) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Volume of Sphere = (4 ÷ 3) × π × (3)³

⇒ Volume of Sphere = (4 ÷ 3) × π × 27 = 36π cm³

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = π × (3)² × h = 9πh

⇒ Since Volume of Sphere = Volume of Cylinder:

⇒ 36π = 9πh

⇒ h = 36 ÷ 9

⇒ h = 4 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a solid object is **melted** and **recast** into another shape, the **total volume** remains the same, provided there is no wastage of material.

Sphere Formulas

Volume = (4/3)πr³ | Total Surface Area = 4πr².

Cylinder Formulas

Volume = πr²h | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h).

Hemisphere Formulas

Volume = (2/3)πr³ | Curved Surface Area = 2πr² | Total Surface Area = 3πr².</p
